markingScheme.criterion: Names a specific item the student themselves sorted into 'Human Impact' during Station 1 (e.g. plastic bottle, factory smokestack, coal power plant) — must be a real item from their own sort, not a generic example.
markingScheme.accept: Any genuine item logged in their Investigation Record under 'Human Impact', by name.
markingScheme.insufficient: A vague reference to 'something I sorted' with no named item.

markingScheme.criterion: Correctly explains the mechanism connecting that item to one of the other three named areas (Ecosystems & Biodiversity, Climate & Weather, or Energy Resources) — e.g. plastic bottle → ocean pollution → harms marine biodiversity; coal power plant → burning fossil fuels → releases greenhouse gases → affects climate.
markingScheme.accept: Any scientifically valid causal chain linking the Human Impact item to a real effect in one of the other three areas; exact wording not required.
markingScheme.insufficient: States the item belongs to another area without explaining how or why.

markingScheme.criterion: States why this cross-area connection matters (e.g. why it shows the four areas of study aren't really separate, or why this connection is significant for the planet/for people).
markingScheme.insufficient: Repeats the mechanism without adding why it matters.

markingScheme.criterion: Identifies one specific, plausible lever from the Footprint Calculator (a specific electricity, transport, or food choice) and states the correct direction of change (e.g. 'walk or cycle instead of driving', 'eat less meat', 'switch off unused lights').
Correctly explains the mechanism by which that specific change reduces resource/energy demand (e.g. less fuel burned, less electricity generated, less land/water used for food production).
Explicitly connects the change to the 'how many Earths' / footprint idea — i.e. states that if enough people made this change, fewer Earths' worth of resources would be needed to support everyone.
markingScheme.insufficient: A generic 'it's good for the environment' statement with no connection to the footprint/Earths concept.

markingInstructions: Mark ONLY the two constructed responses, using the point-by-point marking_scheme carried in each question's marking_context (award each point independently unless it states a dependsOn, in which case only award it if the point it depends on was also awarded) and the rubric's level descriptors, which restate the same points as bands — do not invent extra criteria beyond what is defined.
